    Lap siding · our house standard

    Lap siding: HardiePlank 8.25 in boards

    Overlapping horizontal boards: the classic wood look, in fiber cement made to resist rot, swelling and pests. 301 of our 415 priced jobs used the 8.25 in board.

    Measure the board

    Hang the courses

    Each course shows 7 in of board. Drag, or use the arrow keys.

    Choose the face

    Cedarmill is a cedar wood grain pressed into the face of every board, our default. Smooth is a flat, even face for a crisp, modern line. Also made 5.25 in, 6.25 in and 7.25 in wide.

    What our 415 priced jobs chose

    301of 415 priced jobs used the 8.25 in board

    Each dot is one priced job, not a particular job. Counts: the product named in each of our 415 priced siding job files, 2022–2026. A line naming both textures counts as neither.

    Board and batten · the modern farmhouse look

    Board and batten: vertical panels and battens

    Four-foot HardiePanel sheets hung vertically, with 2.5-inch HardieTrim battens fastened over them: tall, clean lines. 27 of our 415 priced jobs went board and batten.

    Build the wall

    Panel height

    Panels 8 or 10 ft tall. Texture: Cedarmill or smooth (it follows the face you chose above). Spacing as our board and batten job files record it.

    • Panel4 ft wide
    • Batten2.5 in wide
    • Spacing16 in on center

    Shingle and shake · gable accents

    Shingle and shake: gable accents

    Accent walls, corners and gables are part of the “profile and details” that move a siding price. Our own page says most jobs are lap, “with board and batten as an accent”.

    The edges where siding meets roof

    Trim and soffit: corners, fascia, frieze

    We replace soffit and fascia, which protect your roof’s edges and your home’s ventilation, usually in the same job as the siding.

    How far does the job go?

    Look at one part

    Full wrap versus siding faces only is one of the things that moves a siding price: “replacing them with the siding adds to the price and gives a cleaner finish.” We confirm scope and price at the free inspection.

    How a wall goes back together

    The wall, layer by layer

    Whole-house re-sides: tear-off, sheathing fixes where they’re needed, house wrap, siding, trim and paint. Step through it. Typical replacement: 1 to 2 weeks, including paint.

      Six things that move the price

      1. Wall area and storiesMore square footage and second-story walls mean more material, labor and staging.
      2. What’s under the old sidingRotten sheathing found at tear-off gets replaced before new siding goes on.
      3. Whole house or a few wallsWe re-side by the full wall or the whole house, and price only what you need.
      4. Trim, soffit and fasciaReplacing them with the siding adds to the price and gives a cleaner finish.
      5. Paint or ColorPlusSherwin-Williams paint after install, or James Hardie’s factory-baked ColorPlus.
      6. Profile and detailsLap or board and batten, plus accent walls, corners and openings.

      Built for Texas sun, heat and hail

      Your roof gets the rain. Your siding gets everything else.

      UV, triple-digit heat off the walls, spring hail and humidity behind failed caulk. Flashed, sealed and gapped right by an Elite Preferred contractor, James Hardie lasts for decades.

      • Doesn’t warp.UV & heat toughWon’t warp, swell or sag through triple-digit summers.
      • Doesn’t rot.Moisture resistantWon’t rot, swell or soak up water like wood and hardboard.
      • Doesn’t burn.Fire resistantNoncombustible fiber cement. The board itself won’t burn.
      • Doesn’t feed termites.Pest resistantTermites and woodpeckers leave fiber cement alone.
      • Lasts for decades.30-year warrantyNon-prorated from James Hardie when an Elite Preferred contractor installs it.
      30-yearJames Hardie non-prorated siding warranty, when an Elite Preferred contractor installs it.
